title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
goal_html: Students learn to recognize which parts of a web page are attacker-controlled, classify an XSS payload by variant (reflected / stored / DOM-based), and propose the correct output-encoding fix. Ties to LO 5.1.A (identify indicators) and 5.1.B (explain how the vulnerability is exploited).
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation and works through the vulnerable vs. hardened comment-box scenarios, testing each payload and recording whether it "executes" in the sandboxed fake DOM.
  2. For each payload that executed, partners write one sentence naming the XSS variant (reflected, stored, or DOM-based) implied by the delivery mechanism described in the scenario text.
  3. Pairs then write the escaped/encoded version of one payload by hand (e.g., replace < with <, > with >) and confirm in the sim that the encoded version no longer executes.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "attacker" (chooses payloads and predicts whether they will fire), the other is the "defender" (proposes the escaping fix and explains why it neutralizes the payload). Swap roles halfway through.
exit_html: Each student submits: one payload they tested + its XSS variant + the escaped form that defeats it.
